listings.authority: BTG Eddisons / SDL Property Auctions (RICS Regulated)
listings.description:
The subject property comprises the ground floor of an end of terrace building having both an office and a self contained studio apartment.



The property appears to have had various uses over the years. The original use was likely residential, although we understand the ground floor was subsequently in retail use for a number of years. This appears to have been superseded by office use. In 2016, the use of the front part was confirmed by way of a planning application to be a taxi office within the sui generis use class.



The rear part of the ground floor, however, has an independent rear entrance and appears to have been used as a self-contained studio flat since around 2013.



The front part is known as 285 Purley Way and has an entrance on the front elevation, with a metal security shutter. There is a front room and a second room at the rear, with a kitchen installed on the right-hand side. There is a shower room with WC at the rear of the unit. The internal specification of this part is poor, and refurbishment is required prior to occupation.



The unit has a gas-fired boiler providing hot water and central heating, delivered via wall mounted radiators. (not tested)



Purley Way forms part of the A23 and is a major route running on a north-south axis through south London. In a northerly direction it leads towards Streatham and Brixton, whilst in a southerly direction it becomes the M23, just before crossing the M25 motorway at junction 7.



The subject property is located on the east side of Purley Way, on the corner of Jennett Road. This micro-location is characterised by terraces of two storey period housing. Purley Way has two lanes of traffic in either direction, whilst Jennett Road is a short cul de sac.



Purley Way is situated to the west of Croydon town centre, where there is a broad retail offer. However, Purley Way is itself a retail hub, characterised by large retail warehouses.



Nearby occupiers include M&S, Currys, Aldi, Next Home, Carpetright, Sofology, and Hyundai, whilstthere is an Ikea superstore around 0.8 mile to the north.



The nearest rail station is Wandle Park, around 0.3 mile by foot, which provides London Trams services to Wimbledon, East Croydon and various areas of south-east London.

listings.description:
This attractive traditional bay-fronted three-bedroom detached home offers a rare opportunity to acquire a property coming to the open market for the first time in its history, having been cherished by the same family since new. Occupying an elevated position, set back from the road, the property offers excellent potential for a new owner to modernise and personalise whilst retaining the character and proportions of the original home. Offered for sale with no upward chain, the property also provides the benefit of a straightforward and potentially less complicated buying process.



The well-proportioned accommodation briefly comprises; an entrance hall, two generously sized reception rooms, including a bay-fronted living room, together with a fitted kitchen. To the first floor are three bedrooms and a shower room. The property has considerable scope for modernisation, providing an exciting opportunity for purchasers to create a home to their own tastes and requirements.



Externally, the property is particularly well served for parking, with a gated driveway providing multiple vehicle off-road parking, together with a useful car port and garage. The elevated position and set-back frontage add to the property's appeal, whilst the established plot provides a good foundation for further landscaping or enhancement. With its traditional appearance, generous parking provision and excellent potential, this is a property likely to appeal to buyers seeking a detached home with scope to add value.



Spondon is a well-established and popular suburb offering an excellent range of everyday amenities, with a traditional village centre providing convenience stores, independent retailers, cafés, takeaways and other local services. There is a good selection of primary schools locally, together with West Park for secondary education, while larger supermarkets and further retail facilities are available nearby. The area also benefits from good transport links, with Spondon railway station providing services towards Derby and Nottingham, and convenient road connections giving access to the A52 and wider motorway network.

listings.authority: BTG Eddisons / SDL Property Auctions (RICS Regulated)
listings.description:
A freehold development opportunity comprising a Grade II listed former textile mill, built in 1843 in the heart of Macclesfield, offering exceptional potential to create a landmark residential scheme.



The property benefits from approved planning permission for the conversion of the former mill into 30 luxury apartments comprising a range of traditional two-bedroom units alongside a number of spacious three-bedroom duplex penthouses, with associated access and parking (Cheshire East Council Ref: 17/0499M).



The current scheme provides 33 on-site parking spaces. There is also scope to add further apartments, subject to the necessary consents, allowing for additional upside. The Gross Development Value (GDV) is estimated at £7.5 million, presenting a compelling proposition for developers and investors. Crucially, works can commence immediately, Asbestos removal has been carried out by the current owners, significantly reducing initial risk and expediting delivery.



Combining architectural character, scale, and strong residential demand, Albion Mill represents an increasingly rare opportunity to transform an iconic industrial building into high-quality homes.



Originally constructed for Thomas Heapy, a leading figure in Macclesfield celebrated 19th-century silk trade. Architectural highlights include red brick elevations, sandstone detailing, a slate roof, and a prominent central parapet inscribed with Albion Mill 1843 Internally, the building retains many original features, including cast-iron columns and timber beams, offering significant scope for sympathetic restoration.

listings.authority: BTG Eddisons / SDL Property Auctions (RICS Regulated)
listings.description:
A substantial freehold vacant property located along Hinckley Road, Leicester. The building is understood to have been built in the last quarter of the 19th century as an end of terrace dwelling. It is one of four quite substantial properties which would originally have comprised reasonably prestigious dwellings.



Accommodation is arranged over four floors, to include a part basement, part lower ground floor section. In around 1988 the original building was extended to the rear. This part of the building is of single storey construction.



The majority of the building is of solid brick construction, whilst the single storey extension is of cavity brick and block. The roof to the front section cannot be seen from ground level but is apparently pitched and a Google Earth image suggests that it is clad with slate, as is most of the pitched roof covering to the rear single storey section. There are some small flat roofed sections, to include a footway fire escape route from the first floor over the rear single storey section.



To the front elevation is a double height bay window feature.



Apart from a small forecourt area over part of which there are steps leading to the front entrance, and a small area to the rear where the fire escape terminates, the building covers the entire plot.



The accommodation comprises

(Dimensions are in m2 and are approximate).



Ground Floor

Entrance hall 7.3m2

Building total 256.4m2 (2,759 sq. ft.) approx.



Leicester has a population of almost 370,000 (2021 Census) and serves a wider catchment population of over 500,000, being one of the principal cities of the East Midlands, along with Nottingham and Derby. It is about 25 miles south of Nottingham and about 40 miles to the northeast of Birmingham. The city has good access to the motorway network being situated just to the east of the M1, with access from junctions 21 and 22 via the A46 and A50 trunk roads respectively. The M69 motorway, which leads to Coventry and Birmingham, connects with the M1 at junction 21.



Traditionally local employment was dominated by the garment industry, principally textiles, hosiery, and footwear, becoming more diverse following the decline of those traditional industries. Distribution industries are now a major employer along with the service sector and the city's two universities.



Leicester railway station is situated a little over two miles to the east of the property. From Leicester there are direct services to Nottingham, Birmingham New Street and London St Pancras.

An attractive stone built three storey, four bedroom town house forming part of the popular Grade II listed Wynstay Hall Estate development. This well presented property is arranged over ground, first and second floors and offers deceptively spacious accommodation that includes a kitchen, living room, dining room and cloak room / W.C. on the ground floor and four bedrooms (master en-suite) and bathroom over the first and second floors. Externally there is one parking space to the front of the property along with a separate visitors car parking area, large communal gardens and a residents tennis court. listings.street: Pack Horse Inn, Widdop Road, Widdop, Hebden Bridge
listings.authority: BTG Eddisons / SDL Property Auctions (RICS Regulated)
listings.description:
A rare opportunity to acquire a substantial freehold former country inn occupying an outstanding rural position within the Pennines, comprising a historic public house, extensive owner's accommodation, a separate four-bedroom house and a self-contained two-bedroom apartment. Dating back to 1610, the property sits within approximately 0.55 acres and enjoys panoramic views across open moorland, offering significant potential for a variety of redevelopment opportunities, such as a high-end residential scheme, subject to any necessary consents.



The public house has traded successfully for centuries as a destination venue, particularly for food-led trade, benefiting from its position on the Pennine Way and close to Widdop Reservoir. Although the business ceased trading following the departure of the previous tenant in March 2025, the property retains a premises licence and presents an opportunity for a new operator to re-establish the business or explore alternative uses, subject to obtaining any required consents.



The accommodation comprises a traditional bar arranged over two sections with catering kitchen and ancillary areas, together with generous three-bedroom owner's accommodation. Adjoining the pub is a deceptively spacious four-bedroom house with multiple reception rooms, whilst a separate self-contained two-bedroom apartment occupies the first and second floors above the integral garage/store. Externally, the property benefits from customer seating areas, gardens and a substantial car park serving the premises.



Occupying an idyllic countryside setting approximately five miles from Hebden Bridge and eight miles from Colne, the property lies within an area renowned for walking, cycling and outdoor pursuits, attracting visitors throughout the year. Its unique character, sizeable accommodation and picturesque location combine to create an exceptional lifestyle and investment opportunity.
